items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: Next up, we have a song for you requested by Mr. Liu, owner of the Red Lily Pharmacy on Haight Street—Jasmine.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: And here's a little weather report—we've got a bout of extreme weather headed our way; we're talking scorching heatwaves followed up by the one-two punch of a heavy storm front.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: And now, a special announcement: the Silver Gate Restaurant on Grant Avenue will be hosting a banquet at 6 PM tomorrow evening in support of ...
Don't move, please. You have a serious leg injury.
Mr. J, why did you fall from that building?

items.speaker: J
items.text: I ... um? Bru ... Bruce ...?

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: That's right. You remember me? Bruce, yes, Dr. Bruce Liu. I stitched up your arm last month.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Hey, listen—lie still, you're very badly hurt.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Looks like they didn't bother chasing me down here.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: They? Down here? I'm not following.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Just help me up, man. I gotta get back on my feet.
Hongzhi's Clinic

items.speaker: J
items.text: I guess I lost them.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: I don't believe anyone is searching for you.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Not quite true, Doc. J, where have you been off gallivanting this time?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Antony said he hooked me up with a deal, and check it—this is what I got for all my trouble.
It is a grim sight; the young man lies out on a medical bed in a state of brooding agony.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Our Antony? Hmm. "Disaster strikes from within." The doctor just taught me this idiom. I don't have to explain what an idiom is to you, do I, J?

items.speaker: J
items.text: AHHHHHH! AHHH!

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Mr. J ...

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: You have some luck, you know, old boy. That bin you angled yourself into was filled with tattered up old clothes and children's toys from the thrift store.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Not only that, you managed to fall right next to the clinic of the most remarkable surgeon on Haight Street.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: You flatter me, Mr. Pioneer. I am only a back-alley doctor, living off the trust of the locals here and a steady supply of medicinal alcohol.
The doctor attends to J's leg as he speaks, once again preventing the bloodied gangster from rising to his feet with a stern hand.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: What I must do now will be very painful, J. But if you can tough it out, your wounds will heal quickly.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Let me be clear, J. I mean that this is going to be very, very painful.
Not "tough-for-someone-else-but-not-me" painful. Okay, big guy?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Whatever, shove an apple in my mouth then, or a light bulb. Ah no, scratch the light bulb. I remember when Hollick did that, and he was spitting out glass and blood for hours.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Alright, doc. Hit me with it.
He bites down hard on his lip, eyes shut, and breathes deeply.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Okay, just one moment. I'll count to five. Brace yourself.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: One, two ... five!
An unexpected and excruciating moment passes as his leg is twisted back into position.
And then another twist, and just like that, it's done.

items.speaker: J
items.text: I thought Donowitz was the only guy on our block who couldn't count right.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: It's a well-known technique. I've used it myself when I lost a few of my own fingers. I counted two, and then next came five. It's a little less time in the agony of anticipation. Of course, my fingers were made to be reattached.
Bullet-sized beads of sweat mix with the blood dripping from the bite marks on his lower lip. Still, as the moment passes, a smile comes back to J's face.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Hey, that wasn't so ... bad ... after all!

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Come, Mr. J. Let's see if you can put some weight on that leg.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Nice! My leg's back to normal! What the heck did you do to me, doc?!

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Call it traditional Chinese medicine, arcane skill, or whatever suits your fancy. I call it bone-setting, an ancient healing technique practiced for millennia.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Later, I'll concoct some gardenia blood wine for you. If the pain persists, you'll need to dab it on your bruises with some cotton and rub it gently into your skin. Once in the morning and night, each time for a quarter-hour.
The physician cleanses his hands in a nearby basin, dries them with a towel, then crouches by J's side, patting his injured leg.

items.speaker: J
items.text: How long's a quarter-hour again?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Fifteen minutes, nine hundred seconds, or one-fourth of an hour, take your pick.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: How is the pain?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Like nothing, feels as good as new.
He cricks his neck, rotates his wrists, and flexes his limbs like nothing happened.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Excuse me for a second, it seems we have visitors.
Before the doctor can even turn around to address the voices coming from outside, two men rush into the clinic.
One stout and the other skinny, they squeeze through the tight doorframe and crash to the floor.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: J! I heard ya fell from the eighteenth floor! Man, that's some wild stuff!

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Eighteenth floor? It was the eighth floor, the eighth! This joint's only got eight floors, rooftop and all!

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: But that's still high up enough that you ought to be a J pancake, so how come you ain't?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Without the aid of any protective means or arcane skills, a fall from either height would ordinarily be deadly.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Fellas, best not to get hung up on this right now. How'd you two even hear about my "fall"?

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Dr. Liu called the restaurant just before you woke up.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Good thing he did, too.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: I thought it best to let your friends know, Mr. J.
His friends are here, that much is true, but the momentary levity is broken by the arrival of some very much uninvited guests.
Hello, Dr. Liu! We've come to talk with you about our business proposition.
Hey? Doctor? It's the middle of the day, and the door's not locked. Anybody here?

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Darn it, they've come again. Please kindly wait here. I'll speak with them.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Those punks lost or somethin'? Think they can stir up trouble on our block?!

items.speaker: J
items.text: Take it easy, listen to the doc, Becket. Let's chill for a second and scope out the scene.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: You heard the boss, Becket!

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: Ah, welcome, welcome, gentlemen. What can I do for you? Any sprained ankles, injuries? I can treat bruises, fractures, broken bones, colds, and fevers too.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: Don't play dumb with me, Liu!

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: I've got a contract for you. I'm bringing it nice and friendly-like—today. Sign it, and we all walk out of here happy.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: You take the cash, my crew packs up your stuff, and you hit the road.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: And if you don't ...

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Sign here.
The menacing brute pulls out a document from his briefcase, inscribed with words of "generosity," "friendliness," and "sincerity."

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: I'm sorry, gentlemen. But this offer, it's just too low. You can't ask me to surrender my livelihood for this. It's daylight robbery!

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: Robbery? Pfft, our boss has a big heart, taking this ratty drugstore off your hands and still tossing you a little cash! Make the smart decision, doc.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: J, I smell somethin' fishy goin' on out there.
Before Hollick can finish, J strides out, flinging aside the clinic's yellowed curtain and stepping into the front hall.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Remember, don't start throwing punches, at least not until they do.
His two friends follow closely behind him, the burly Hollick and the nimble Becket flanking J's imposing figure.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Oh, this does not look like it will end well. Best I call on Sheriff Blackhand.

items.speaker: J
items.text: You think you can get away with strong-arming folks around here?

items.speaker: J
items.text: He ain't looking to deal with trash like you.

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: Watch it, punk.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: Trash? Say that again, kid, and I swear you'll be in the trash tomorrow morning, wrapped up in a Persian rug.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Yes, that's right, the Red Lily Clinic. Connect me directly with Sheriff Blackhand, if you would. There's likely to be an incident here that demands his immediate attention.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Dr. Liu ain't signing anything today, pal.
It's three against two, or perhaps only one, as the would-be mobster withdraws meekly behind his muscle.
Hollick and Becket step forward, presenting a solid wall that shields the doctor behind them.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: What is it, little man? You don't wanna get those soft hands of yours dirty?

items.speaker: Henchman
items.text: How about you check out these mitts, kid?
The bald strongman seizes Becket by the collar, his fist held back and taut like a slingshot ready to launch.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Becket!

items.speaker: J
items.text: I'll admit it, bub. You've got a pair of monsters there.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Cool it, Hollick.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: Put your hands down, moron. We don't want to make another mess for the boss to clean up! Let's get out of here!
Becket wriggles free from the brute's grip and snorts up at him, taking time to straighten out his clothes as he falls back behind Hollick.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: I think we should all take a step back, gents. The doctor's calendar here says today's not a good day for a brawl.
The mannequin squeezes in between the two sides, raising his hands rigidly as if to create a barrier.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: There's never a good day for fighting! Peace is precious, gentlemen.
The tense standoff grows awkward, and the unwelcome pair of thugs slink back toward the door.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: This ain't over.

items.speaker: Henchman Leader
items.text: Liu, we tossed you a bone, but we won't be so generous next time. Come on, you big lug. We gotta get out of here.
The unwelcome guests leave their threats hanging as they fall back through the clinic's door.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Well done, gents. It seems you've won, for the moment.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: J, did you know those guys?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Yeah, they were there last night. When Antony brought me up to the rooftop here to make a deal with their boss. Or so he said—

items.speaker: J
items.text: But it was a setup!

items.speaker: J
items.text: Their boss handed me a box of cash, wanted me to sell Haight Street out to him, or else I wasn't going to leave that rooftop alive.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Lucky for me, my best girl had my back, and we found our own way down.
The swordsmith pats the colossal weapon behind him with pride.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: Your "own way down" being an eight-story drop slowed only by your sword, as I understand.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: So then, these men are in the employ of this Hung San. Doctor, might I presume you are far from the only business to have been approached with this "generous offer"?

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: *sigh*

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: I'm afraid so. Not just that, they've also been muscling out the migrant workers. Seems they don't want anyone left on Haight Street.

items.speaker: J
items.text: What?!
A little late to the action, the door swings open, and a familiar face walks through confidently.

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: Alright, I'm here. Now someone want to tell me what sort of "incident" was kicking off here?

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: J, Hollick, Becket ... Should have known you three would be here.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: I made the call, Sheriff. Fortunately, the matter was resolved without bloodshed.

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: You going to tell me what happened?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Really, Blackhand? You're going to tell me our sheriff's got no idea what's going on in his own backyard?

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: Zip it, kid. And you're one to talk. From the look of you, I'm guessing these Grant Avenue boys already got the drop on you.

items.speaker: Dr. Liu
items.text: They want to tear down the street so they can build some kind of entertainment complex. They've already pressured a few shops to close.

items.speaker: J
items.text: An entertainment complex. Jeez, and I suppose in their heads, we'll all just sign up to wait tables for their crumbs? Where are the kids going to leave their tags on a monstrosity like that?

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: You know I'd rather you weren't encouraging the kids to plaster every wall with that crap. It's a pain in my ass to get it cleaned up.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Hey, it's street art, man, street art! We gotta protect the arts, don't we?!

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: Yeah, yeah. Whatever, I've got bigger things on my plate. And so do you. Listen, I know most folk working around here don't have their papers, and I've got orders from up-top to come down hard on them.

items.speaker: J
items.text: You gonna follow through?

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: Gonna? Ha, you've been out for a bit, haven't you? We've already wrangled them up by the dozens, and they're gonna stay there until they're deported.
Deportation. A dreadful term, worse than a two-week-old sour cucumber beef roll.

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: I'll tell you what, though, J, I hate this new crew just as much as you do. They're making a mess of this district, and now I've got city hall squeezing me. So you gonna tell me what you know?

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: This block's got its own rules, and I know you boys have kept things nice and low-key, but if things change ... Dammit, I don't want to have to play rough here.

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: For now, I've got to make appearances. So, if you want your street back, you gotta figure out who these new guys are and who's backing their operation.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: If I've picked up what the sheriff is saying, J, it sounds like you handle the gang, and he'll restore freedom to our neighborhood friends.

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: The dummy's got it right. I'm asking you to make my life a little easier, and find out who's backing these guys.

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: No hard feelings, J. You've got your problems, and I've got mine. Me, you, Becket, Hollick ... we all agree on this—priority one is taking out these gangsters.
The sheriff glances at Hollick and Becket.

items.speaker: J
items.text: I'm in, Sheriff.

items.speaker: Pioneer
items.text: It seems to be the best way forward for us.

items.speaker: Becket
items.text: Whatever you say, J.

items.speaker: Hollick
items.text: Boss, you say jump, I'm jumpin'!

items.speaker: Sheriff Blackhand
items.text: Great. Get it done.
